_readme: Registry of independent model testers — every entry below was actually fetched (curl or a headless browser where a site is JS-rendered) on the date in `as_of`, not assumed from memory. Design + the rule this file exists to serve: the AI never ranks a model. Ranking is planned to come from agreement across the testers named here, plus human votes, plus real usage (OpenRouter) — never from a judgment this codebase makes up. `mapping` reports how many of this catalog's models (data/models.json) each tester's feed names contain, using a throwaway matcher (scripts/_audit/map-names.mjs) that only strips KNOWN reasoning-effort/date suffixes before comparing — it never guesses a fuzzy match. `licence.class` is one of display-ok (redistributable), signal-only (usable to inform an internal decision, never republished raw), banned (explicit terms or copyright notice against reuse), or unknown (no terms found — never guessed). `verdict` is this audit's own call: use | signal-only | exclude, each with a one-line reason in that tester's own `verdict_reason`.

testers.name: Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub

licence.quote: free to use, distribute, and reproduce provided the source and authors are credited under the Creative Commons Attribution license — Epoch AI's own runs. 'This hub also includes data sourced from external projects, which retains its original licensing' (same page, checked 2026-09-07): Aider Polyglot and Terminal-Bench are confirmed Apache-2.0 via their own repos; every other `*_external` set's upstream terms are unstated here — see mapping.per_benchmark.

research: ARC-AGI-2 (mirrored — see arc-prize entry for the primary source)
vision: Video-MME (mirrored; 0 catalog models matched — see notes)

testers.refresh: rolling; Epoch adds/updates CSVs on its own schedule. Already wired into this repo's Collect pass via scripts/collect-epoch.mjs, which proposes but never writes.
testers.independence: Runs several evals itself (GPQA Diamond, SimpleQA Verified, SWE-bench Verified, FrontierMath, MATH L5) but mirrors others published by interested parties: CursorBench is published by Cursor, which ships its own coding model; WebDev Arena and Video-MME are community/third-party leaderboards Epoch mirrors, not runs; OpenAI funded Epoch's FrontierMath with dataset access, disclosed only after the fact. https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/use-this-data
testers.notes: Corrected 2026-09-07 (brain v2 step 1 continued): the prior pass only counted CursorBench's own ladder (15/74) and missed that benchmark_data.zip holds 80 benchmark CSVs (82 files minus 2 metadata-only ones). Recomputed feed-wide with scripts/_audit/map-names.mjs on every CSV's 'Model version' column: 926 raw names, 902 after slug-dedup, 37 distinct catalog models matched — independently re-derived and cross-checked against the full-feed union, both agree. 36 of the 37 are covered by the 14 per_benchmark sets above; the 37th (qwen3-coder-plus) only appears in ale_bench_external.csv, a set outside this catalog's 10 task ids, so it isn't in the table. video_mme_external.csv (50 feed models) is this catalog's only Video-MME/vision source but matches 0 catalog models, noted inline in `tasks.vision` rather than in the table; live_bench_external.csv (52 feed models) also matches 0 and doesn't map to any of the 10 task ids, so it's absent from both `tasks` and the table. Checked why both are 0 — not a matcher bug: live_bench_external's newest rows are gpt-5.1/o3-mini/claude-3.7-era (frozen before this catalog's current models existed); video_mme_external is a dedicated open-source video-LLM leaderboard that has never carried a current frontier model. FrontierMath stays in `independence` above for its disclosed OpenAI conflict but is dropped from `tasks` — it doesn't map to any of this catalog's 10 task ids either.

testers.name: LiveBench

licence.quote: the GitHub repo (LiveBench/livebench) carries an Apache License (copied from lm-sys/FastChat), but that covers the evaluation CODE — no separate licence or terms statement was found on livebench.ai itself for the live table_*.csv this audit fetched, so the DATA's own terms are left unknown rather than assumed from the code licence

coding: Coding category (code_generation, code_completion, python, javascript, typescript)
research: Reasoning category (connections, logic_with_navigation, zebra_puzzle, spatial, theory_of_mind); Math category (AMPS_Hard, math_comp, olympiad, integrals_with_game)

testers.refresh: irregular. The site's own release-date selector (read out of its JS bundle) tops out at 2026-06-25 — about 2.5 months stale as of this audit — even though the question-bank changelog shows edits into January 2026. Its HuggingFace dataset mirror (livebench/model_judgment, livebench/model_answer) is far more stale: last updated 2025-04-07 and 2024-10-22 respectively, confirmed via the HF commits API — do not use that HF mirror as a model-score source; the live table_*.csv the site itself serves is the current one.
testers.independence: Run by the LiveBench team (academic + Abacus.AI-affiliated maintainers per GitHub commit authorship); questions are deliberately refreshed to resist training-set contamination. No known eval-for-hire conflict found. https://livebench.ai/
testers.notes: Best mapping rate of any benchmark tester audited (32/56). The public site is a create-react-app SPA that fetches `./table_<date>.csv` (dates found by reading the site's own compiled JS, not documented anywhere) — genuinely machine-readable once you know the filename pattern, but not a stated/stable API; treat as discovered, not published, same caveat this repo already carries for OpenRouter's rankings endpoints. A documented 'agentic coding' category exists per the project's changelog (added 2025-05-30, SWE-Agent/Mini-SWE-Agent harness) but its columns were not present in the table_2026_06_25.csv pulled here — likely served as a separate export not fetched in this pass; flagged for follow-up rather than guessed at.

Only o4-mini matched cleanly. Licence unknown (not banned, not confirmed open) is why this sits at signal-only rather than use, despite being a real, machine-readable, live-fetched feed.

testers.refresh: rolling — several entries carried a 'NEW' badge as of today (2026-09-07); no fixed cadence stated. A 'Show Deprecated Leaderboards' toggle implies boards get retired over time.
testers.independence: Scale AI is a major commercial vendor of data-labeling, RLHF, and evaluation services to frontier labs (OpenAI, Meta, Google, and others) — the same conflict class as Artificial Analysis and Vals AI, arguably deeper given the breadth of Scale's lab contracts. The page itself invites vendors in: 'If you'd like to add your model to this leaderboard... contact leaderboards@scale.com.' https://labs.scale.com/leaderboard
testers.notes: Sample drawn only from the homepage's top-3-per-benchmark cards (26 benchmarks x ~3 rows); full per-benchmark rankings sit one click deeper behind 'View Full Ranking' and were not fetched in this pass — real mapped/feed numbers across full tables would likely differ from 13/44. Several unmatched names bundle the agent/harness into the model string ('GPT-5.5 (mini-SWE-agent) xhigh') in a way this audit's suffix-stripper doesn't parse — a naming-convention gap, not a data gap. 'All rights reserved' plus the direct lab-contract conflict keeps this at signal-only despite genuinely broad, current, catalog-matching coverage.

testers.name: ARC Prize Foundation — ARC-AGI-2 Evaluations

licence.quote: "no part of the Services and no Content or Marks may be copied, reproduced, aggregated, republished, uploaded, posted, publicly displayed, encoded, translated, transmitted, distributed, sold, licensed, or otherwise exploited for any commercial purpose whatsoever, without our express prior written permission" (Terms and Conditions, last updated 2024-06-03, checked 2026-09-07) — permission requested from team@arcprize.org 2026-08-22, no reply on file.

research: ARC-AGI-2 semi-private evaluation (score + cost-per-task by model, run by the ARC Prize Foundation itself)

testers.refresh: rolling — the Foundation updates this JSON as new model runs land; the same file also carries older ARC-AGI-1 (v1_*) evaluations alongside the ARC-AGI-2 (v2_*/v3_*) ones.
testers.independence: Nonprofit that designs, runs, and pays for the ARC-AGI evaluation itself rather than selling evaluation services to the labs it grades — no vendor pays for placement here. https://arcprize.org/about
testers.notes: Class is signal-only pending the 2026-08-22 permission request to team@arcprize.org (no reply on file) — arcprize.org's terms ban republishing for any commercial purpose without written permission, so this feed can inform an internal decision but nothing from it gets displayed raw until permission lands. Mapped live via scripts/_audit/map-names.mjs against the 247 distinct modelId strings in evaluations.json: only 12 distinct catalog models matched, and that's a real undercount, not the true rate. This feed's ids use a hyphen-joined vendor prefix ('anthropic-claude-fable-5-1-high', 'google-gemini-3-7-flash-high') that scripts/auto-refresh.mjs's stripProviderPrefix doesn't strip — its PROVIDER_PREFIX regex only recognizes a vendor prefix followed by '/' or '.', not '-'. Left unfixed here (out of scope for a research-only pass; a real fix belongs in auto-refresh.mjs, not this throwaway audit script). Epoch's arc_agi_2_external.csv mirrors this same ARC-AGI-2 data and matches 22/203 with the same unmodified matcher (see epoch-ai entry) — a partial cross-check that the true match rate on this feed is well above 12/247. GitHub repos, both confirmed via the GitHub API 2026-09-07: arcprize/arc-agi-benchmarking (MIT — harness/config code only, no results data) and arcprize/ARC-AGI-2 (Apache-2.0 — the dataset itself, not the leaderboard results).
